clue.text: In which some venerable figures still endure the rubs of life

definitions.text: In which some venerable figures still endure the rubs of life

parts.words: In which some venerable figures still endure the rubs of life
parts.note: church memorials engraved with knights and ladies are still rubbed onto paper by visitors, so their figures keep enduring rubs

explanation.surface: A reflection on how old dignitaries keep suffering life's knocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubs of life' sounds like life's hardships, but here it means brass rubbings, taken by pressing paper on engraved memorial plates in English churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental plates of engraved metal set into church floors carry effigies of the long dead and are a favourite subject for rubbings.

clue.text: A crooked joint, but utilitarian, man

parts.note: bent means crooked
a ham is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A bent joint is still useful to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Bentham was the founding philosopher of utilitarianism; 'A' and 'but' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The English philosopher who argued for the greatest happiness of the greatest number founded utilitarianism.

clue.text: Lad's love for a queen

definitions.meaning: lad's love is the old country name for southernwood, a shrubby herb
a queen of ancient Caria bore this name

explanation.surface: A boy's affection for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lad's love' looks like a boy's crush but is a plant name; the genus covers southernwood and wormwood.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus including southernwood, called lad's love, shares its name with a famous ruler of Caria.

clue.text: A point of graceful writing ?

parts.note: a pen point is meant, while the surface suggests a mark of literary style

explanation.surface: A question about what makes elegant prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a feature of style but is the tip of a fountain pen of the stylograph type, its name echoing 'style'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylograph is a fountain pen with a fine tubular point, and the short name sounds like literary style.

clue.text: Was he waggish with Iris, dashing with Dot ?

definitions.text: Was he waggish with Iris, dashing with Dot ?

parts.words: Was he waggish with Iris, dashing with Dot ?
parts.note: a person sending messages wags flags, flashes an iris-shuttered lamp, and taps out Morse dashes and dots

explanation.surface: A gossip asks whether a man flirted with two women called Iris and Dot.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris and Dot look like girls' names; flags are wagged, a signal lamp has an iris shutter, and Morse code is dots and dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sends messages by flag, lamp or Morse code is a military communications operator.

clue.text: Old watch, a proper simple one

definitions.meaning: before police forces, a night watchman in London was nicknamed by this name
a 'proper Charlie' is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A description of an antique timepiece that is plain and correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but means a watchman; 'a proper Charlie' is everyday British for a complete fool, the spelling here being the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was slang both for an old-time night watchman and for a simpleton.

clue.text: " Where ignorant armies — by night " (Arnold).

parts.note: the missing verb of the last line of Matthew Arnold's poem Dover Beach

explanation.surface: A quotation from Victorian verse with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is the close of Matthew Arnold's 'Dover Beach': armies meeting in the dark fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies that fight come into violent conflict, which is the verb Arnold used.

clue.text: I, Abe 26, am liable to be transferred

definitions.text: I, Abe 26, am liable to be transferred

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order, as property moves from owner to owner

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, the surname of the ballad heroine Barbara

explanation.surface: A man named Abe Allen admits he could be moved to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be transferred' rearranges I, ABE and ALLEN (the answer to 26 across); the whole clue also defines, since what can be transferred is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that can be sold or handed to another owner is capable of being transferred.

clue.text: At one roughly, or shortly before

definitions.text: At one roughly, or shortly before

parts.words: At one roughly, or shortly before
parts.note: the midday meal is taken around one o'clock or a little earlier, and the word is itself a shortening of a longer one

explanation.surface: A rough time given for an appointment: one o'clock or just before.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is usually eaten at about one in the afternoon.

clue.text: One's up to the eyes in the East

definitions.text: One's up to the eyes in the East

parts.words: One's up to the eyes in the East
parts.note: a veil worn by some Muslim women covers the face up to the eyes

explanation.surface: Someone in Asia is overwhelmed with work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to the eyes' sounds like busy, but describes a veil that covers the face below the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: This double veil, worn in parts of the Muslim world, hides the face apart from the eyes.

clue.text: Gilbert gaga ?

parts.note: Gilbert the Filbert, in an old music-hall song, is the colonel of the Knuts, and a filbert is a hazel kernel, so he would be crazy in two senses

explanation.surface: A question whether someone named Gilbert has gone senile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gilbert the Filbert' was a 1914 music-hall song about a dandy, a 'knut'; a filbert is a hazelnut, so the word for crazy also fits him literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means crazy or mad, and the adjective also describes something full of or tasting of kernels.

clue.text: Allowances about to expire for alterations of road levels

indicators.note: the word allowances goes round the other piece, so it sits about it

parts.note: grants are allowances of money
to expire is to die

explanation.surface: Grants nearly running out are being spent on changing road heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expire' and 'allowances' suggest money running out, but the definition is the closing phrase about road levels; 'about' signals the container and 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slopes are changes in the level of a road as it rises or falls.

clue.text: Sweet spot but no way to it for the medico

parts.note: home, as in 'home sweet home', is the sweet spot
O is nought, nothing
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Someone longs to get home but cannot find the road there to fetch the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet spot' plays on 'home sweet home'; 'but', 'to it for the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of the alternative medical system of tiny doses is a kind of doctor, a medico.

clue.text: In Scotland not to sing under your breath, old man

parts.note: na is the Scots form of not
to hum is to sing with closed lips

explanation.surface: A Scottish father refuses to sing quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old man' is an Old Testament figure: the minor prophet who gives his name to a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a minor prophet of the Old Testament, so a man from old scripture.

clue.text: They rise stiff in their shrouds

definitions.text: They rise stiff in their shrouds

parts.words: They rise stiff in their shrouds
parts.note: shrouds are the ropes bracing a ship's tall spars, which stand stiff among them

explanation.surface: Corpses rising rigid in their burial cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a ghoulish resurrection; shrouds are also the sets of ropes running from a ship's mastheads to its sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall upright spars on a ship are braced by rigging ropes called shrouds.

clue.text: Crafty 'suit it makes

parts.note: the canvas makes the sails, the suit a sailing craft wears

explanation.surface: A cunning lawsuit someone brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like cunning but means of a boat, and a ship's 'suit' of sails is made from this canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy canvas is the fabric from which a vessel's sails are made.

clue.text: The dark of the light

parts.note: the black soot that an oil lamp gives off

explanation.surface: A paradox: the darkness belonging to light.
explanation.definitionFit: This pigment is fine carbon collected from the smoke of burning oil, the soot a lamp produces.

clue.text: Unpobblelike bird living on a tree

parts.note: the mistle thrush is often called simply the mistle
Edward Lear's Pobble has no toes, so one unlike him has a toe

explanation.surface: A bird unlike Lear's creature perches in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's nonsense poem 'The Pobble Who Has No Toes', the Pobble lost his toes, so 'Unpobblelike' gives TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen is a parasite that grows on the branches of trees such as apple and oak.

clue.text: Pedicurist to royalty

parts.note: the slave in the old tale pulled a thorn from the paw of a lion, the king of beasts

explanation.surface: A foot specialist with a royal warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'royalty' is the lion, king of beasts; the runaway slave of the legend removed a thorn from its foot and was later spared by it in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman slave of legend tended a lion's injured paw, treating the foot of the king of beasts.

clue.text: London dons' local ?

parts.note: Spanish gentlemen are dons, and a famous pub on Hampstead Heath in London bears their nationality as its name

explanation.surface: Which pub in London do the university fellows drink in?
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like university teachers, but a Don is a Spanish gentleman; the Spaniards Inn is a well-known old pub in Hampstead, north London, a 'local' being a regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Men from Spain are dons, and a historic London inn on Hampstead Heath has that plural nationality for its name.

clue.text: Elementary to sound such a foolish little girl

indicators.note: the words are said aloud and heard as the chemical name

parts.note: silly is foolish, and Con is a pet form of Constance or Connie

explanation.surface: A girl is told it is simple to sound so foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' looks like simple but means being a chemical element; 'such a' is part of the leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: This non-metal is a chemical element, number fourteen, so it is something elementary.

clue.text: Not such a green man though

definitions.text: Not such a green man though

parts.words: Not such a green man though
parts.note: one older is less green, less inexperienced, though the tree of that name is green

explanation.surface: Someone saying a person is less naive than supposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' means inexperienced: an older person is less so, yet the shrub of that name is green, hence 'though'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone senior is more experienced, and the word also names a green-leaved shrub with black berries.

clue.text: Has a grouse but no piano from donors

indicators.note: no piano says the letter for piano is left out of the gifts

parts.note: presents are things given by donors
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Someone complains that donors gave no piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes P from PRESENTS; 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a grouse, a grievance, is to feel bitter or aggrieved at something.

clue.text: Domino-time ?

parts.note: the word goes before 'Domino' and before 'Time' to give titles of two old operettas

explanation.surface: Is it time for a game of dominoes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lilac Domino' and 'Lilac Time' were popular operettas of the early twentieth century; the clue gives just the words that follow the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub's name is the first word of two operetta titles, one ending in Domino and one in Time.

clue.text: I am entering a continental sleeper at the terminus

indicators.note: entering says the words I am go inside the bed

parts.note: lit is French for bed
I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: Someone boards a sleeping car on a European train at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' suggests a night train, but 'continental' points to the French word for a bed; 'at the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An end point or boundary is a terminus.

clue.text: Bogs might be right full of them

definitions.text: Bogs might be right full of them

indicators.note: these words say the letters could become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Marshes could well be teeming with these big amphibians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges BOGS, R (right) and FULL; the whole clue is also the definition, since marshes may be full of the creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Large croaking amphibians live in marshy ground, so wet bogs teem with them.

clue.text: Off with their heads in the cause of good health !

definitions.text: Off with their heads in the cause of good health !

parts.words: Off with their heads in the cause of good health !
parts.note: drinks with frothy heads are swallowed when toasting someone's health

explanation.surface: An executioner's cry framed as a health measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off with their heads' sounds like a beheading order; frothy pints have heads, drunk down in a toast of good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Pints of ale have frothy heads and are drunk in toasts to good health.

clue.text: A boy is left money abroad

indicators.note: is left means the word is departs from the boy's name

parts.note: Francis is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy is bequeathed money while overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like bequeathed but means gone: IS leaves FRANCIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency unit of France, Belgium and Switzerland, so foreign money.

clue.text: A part for make-up

parts.note: a piece that goes into the makeup of a whole, while the surface suggests theatrical cosmetics

explanation.surface: An actor's role that calls for greasepaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' and 'make-up' suggest the theatre, but the sense is a constituent piece of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is one of the parts that together make up a whole.

clue.text: Barbara is a backward little Dickensian

indicators.note: backward means the name of the girl is written from end to start

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: Someone called Barbara is a shy, slow child from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Allen is the heroine of a famous traditional ballad, so her surname completes 'Barbara'; 'backward' turns NELL into LLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cruel maiden of the old folk ballad is called Barbara by first name and this by surname.

clue.text: Nicks tench so

annotationWithheld.why: Nicks tench so (7): TENCH SO is an anagram of the answer but no word but the definition 'Nicks' could signal the anagram, so one word would do two jobs

clue.text: Scrubs in duty's name

definitions.meaning: to scrub a plan is to cut it out or cancel it
a tax on home goods is called by this name

explanation.surface: Someone scrubbing floors in the name of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubs' looks like cleaning but means cuts out; 'in' is a link word. The plural noun names the duties levied on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut out is the verb sense; the noun is the name of taxes charged on goods made at home.
